findings.evidence: Basic.lean:315-318: `refine MeasureTheory.Integrable.integrableOn ?_; simpa only [pow_zero, one_mul] using h.momentIntegrable 0 i Q2` — the `Integrable` is derived, then discarded.
findings.fix: State `Regularity.integrable {f : Pdf Flavor} (h : Regularity f) (i) (Q2) : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x : ℝ => f i x Q2)` and write `(hr.integrable s Q2).integrableOn` at the single use site (`PartonModel.lean:166`).
findings.issue: `Regularity.integrableOn` proves global `Integrable (fun x => f i x Q2)` (`simpa only [pow_zero, one_mul] using h.momentIntegrable 0 i Q2`) and then weakens it to `IntegrableOn (Set.Icc 0 1)` inside the lemma, so the stronger fact is unavailable to any consumer needing a different set or global integrability.

findings.evidence: PartonModel.lean:103 `g1 x Q2 := (1 / 2) * ∑ f, charge f ^ 2 * (Δ (.quark f) x Q2 + Δ (.antiquark f) x Q2)` — no `.gluon`; Positivity.lean:113-126 documents `SpinDensity` as the per-quark-flavour forward quark-nucleon helicity-amplitude matrix.
findings.fix: Restrict the hypotheses to the species that occur: `∀ f x Q2, (x < 0 ∨ 1 < x) → Δ (.quark f) x Q2 = 0 ∧ Δ (.antiquark f) x Q2 = 0` and likewise for measurability/integrability, and let the spin-density version constrain only the quark and antiquark entries of Δ, leaving `Δ .gluon` free; keep `assumptions_partonModel_of_regularity` (full `PDF.Regularity` bundle) as the ergonomic wrapper.
findings.issue: Hypotheses are quantified over all of `Species Flavor` though `partonModel` reads only `Δ (.quark f)` and `Δ (.antiquark f)` (line 103); the gluon instance is never used. Worst for `assumptions_partonModel_helicityPdfOfSpinDensity`, which takes `ρ : Species Flavor → ℝ → ℝ → SpinDensity` plus `SpinDensityAssumptions ρ`: it demands a positive-semidefinite quark-nucleon helicity-amplitude matrix for the gluon, so a Δ whose gluon entry is defined independently of any `SpinDensity` is outside the theorem's reach even though Δg does not enter g₁. Same over-quantification at lines 122 (`hΔ`), 130-132 (`hm`, `hi`), 150-153, 184-185 and 228.

summary: Two hypotheses sit below the natural level: `Regularity.integrableOn` discards the global integrability its own proof produces, and every parton-model lemma quantifies over all species including the gluon, which `partonModel` never reads — which makes the spin-density theorem inapplicable to any helicity set whose gluon entry is not read off a quark-nucleon spin-density matrix.
